name: Thomas R. Suozzi

data_centers.summary: No public statements on data centers found as of Sept 2026. Suozzi voted against the SPEED Act permitting bill and is an original cosponsor of the Energy Bills Relief Act, a clean-energy tax credit and grid bill, but neither is a data center position. He has not cosponsored any of the House data center bills (Ratepayer Protection Act, Data Center Transparency Act, Power for the People Act or the AI Data Center Moratorium Act).

evidence.title: Original cosponsor: Energy Bills Relief Act (H.R. 7977)
evidence.what_it_shows: A House Democratic bill to restore clean energy tax credits, expand LIHEAP and modernize the grid; it is about electricity costs generally, not data centers.

evidence.title: Voted Nay on the SPEED Act (H.R. 4776), House roll call 356
evidence.what_it_shows: Opposed the Republican permitting-reform bill that backers said would speed energy and infrastructure projects; a party-line vote, not a data center statement.

ai_risk.summary: Suozzi backs targeted rules against specific AI harms. He cosponsored the TAKE IT DOWN Act and the DEFIANCE Act on sexual deepfakes, the QUIET Act requiring AI robocalls to identify themselves, and the NO FAKES Act on AI voice and face copies. No statements found on frontier AI safety, licensing or a pause.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: DEFIANCE Act of 2025 (H.R. 3562)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports letting victims sue over AI-made sexual deepfakes.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: TAKE IT DOWN Act (H.R. 633)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports criminal penalties and fast takedowns for nonconsensual real or AI-faked intimate images.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: QUIET Act (H.R. 1027)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports requiring AI-voiced robocalls to disclose they are AI and raising fines.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: NO FAKES Act of 2024 (H.R. 9551, 118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a legal right to stop unauthorized AI copies of a person's voice or likeness.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Facial Recognition to Protect Children Act (H.R. 9706)
evidence.what_it_shows: Favors face-scan age checks to keep kids out of adult online products; shows comfort with using AI tools for child safety.

tech_regulation.summary: Suozzi favors targeted tech rules, especially for kids and scams. He cosponsored the Kids Online Safety Act, COPPA 2.0 and Sammy's Law, robocall and romance-scam bills, and a ban on Chinese-linked connected-car tech, and he voted for the 2024 TikTok divest-or-ban bill. In an August 2026 op-ed with Scott Galloway he blamed tech platforms built to polarize.

evidence.title: Op-ed with Scott Galloway: Mandatory service can renew young people's faith in America (Chicago Tribune, posted on suozzi.house.gov)
evidence.quote: A transfer of wealth from young to old, an education system that ill-equips young people for today’s economy and technology platforms engineered to polarize us have produced a generation of Americans who no longer believe in America.
evidence.what_it_shows: Frames social media platforms as a cause of social harm, consistent with his support for kids' online safety rules.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Kids Online Safety Act (H.R. 7891, 118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed the main bill requiring platforms to protect minors from harmful content and addictive design.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Children and Teens' Online Privacy Protection Act (H.R. 7890, 118th Congress)
evidence.what_it_shows: Backed stronger privacy limits on collecting kids' and teens' data.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Sammy's Law (H.R. 2657)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports forcing big platforms to let parents use third-party safety apps.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Connected Vehicle Security Act of 2026 (H.R. 8730)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports banning connected-car tech from companies tied to China, Russia, Iran or North Korea.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Foreign Robocall Elimination Act (H.R. 6152)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports a crackdown on overseas scam robocalls.

evidence.title: Voted Yea on H.R. 7521, Protecting Americans from Foreign Adversary Controlled Applications Act (TikTok divest-or-ban), House roll call 86 of 2024
evidence.what_it_shows: Supported forcing TikTok's Chinese owner to divest or face a US ban.

preemption.summary: No statement found on federal preemption of state AI laws. Suozzi did not sign the November 2025 Matsui letter or the December 2025 Clarke letter against an AI moratorium, and he has not cosponsored the GUARDRAILS Act. His vote against H.R. 1 was a vote on the whole tax-and-spending bill, not on the moratorium.

evidence.title: Voted Nay on House passage of H.R. 1 (contained the 10-year moratorium on state AI laws), House roll call 145
evidence.what_it_shows: He opposed the reconciliation bill that carried the state AI-law moratorium, but the vote was on the entire bill, so it is weak evidence on preemption.

china_chips.summary: Suozzi leans hawkish on China and chips. He cosponsored the Chip Security Act to put location tracking on advanced AI chips, joined the House China Select Committee in June 2026 saying the US is in a strategic competition with the Chinese Communist Party, and voted for the TikTok divest-or-ban bill. He also backs tax credits for US chip factories. No specific statement found on Nvidia H20 or H200 sales.

evidence.what_it_shows: Supports requiring built-in location verification on advanced AI chips to catch smuggling to China.

evidence.quote: We must recognize that we are in a strategic competition with the Chinese Communist Party. This competition affects our economy, our national security, and our geopolitical standing in the world.
evidence.what_it_shows: Frames China as a strategic competitor across economy and security, the committee that handles chip export questions.

china_chips.summary: Meeks is one of the House's strongest voices for tight chip export controls. As top Democrat on Foreign Affairs he wrote the RESTRICT Act to ban H200 and other advanced AI chip sales to China, used his statutory power with Sen. Warren to force Commerce to hand over H200 license records, cosponsored the AI OVERWATCH Act giving Congress a veto over chip sales, and repeatedly warned against using export controls as bargaining chips in trade talks.

evidence.title: Sponsor: RESTRICT Act (H.R. 6879), to prohibit sales of the most advanced AI chips to China
evidence.what_it_shows: His own bill would deny export licenses for advanced AI chips to China and other arms-embargoed countries while easing exports to trusted US data centers abroad.

evidence.title: Press release: Meeks Introduces Bill to Block Sales of Advanced AI Chips to China (RESTRICT Act)
evidence.quote: President Trump’s decision to sell H200s to China further proves that national security is for sale under this administration.
evidence.what_it_shows: Directly opposes the H200 sales and wants them prohibited by law.

evidence.title: Press release: Meeks and Warren invoke Export Control Reform Act to require Commerce to turn over H200 license information
evidence.quote: Approving licenses for items like NVIDIA’s H200 chips, which the Justice Department recently described as ‘integral to modern military applications,’ would be deeply at odds with the policy that Congress articulated in ECRA.
evidence.what_it_shows: Used ranking-member powers to scrutinize and slow H200 license approvals.

evidence.title: Nextgov: Lawmakers worry over new rule that will allow sales of Nvidia's H200 chips to China (House Foreign Affairs hearing)
evidence.quote: The president has said he will not approve H200 licenses for bad actors in China. While this does not allay concerns about smuggling and diversions, I am also skeptical that the administration will pick the right customers from the start
evidence.what_it_shows: Called the H200 rule a strategic mistake that degrades national security and doubted the administration's vetting of Chinese buyers.

evidence.title: The Hill: House panel advances AI chip export control bill (AI OVERWATCH Act markup)
evidence.quote: While I wish the bill before us today directly prohibited the sale of H200s, it nevertheless puts in place robust guardrails that would delay those sales and allow for congressional review and oversight going forward
evidence.what_it_shows: Voted to advance the bill giving Congress arms-sale-style review of AI chip exports, while saying he wanted an outright H200 ban.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: AI OVERWATCH Act (H.R. 6875)
evidence.what_it_shows: Supports giving Congress the power to block advanced AI chip sales to China and other risky countries.

evidence.title: Meeks, Warren Statement on Trump Administration's Approval of Advanced AI Chip Sales to China

evidence.what_it_shows: After reviewing the first H200 license, called for bipartisan legislation to keep advanced technology from China.

evidence.title: Cosponsor: Export Controls Enforcement Act (H.R. 4505)
